# Known failures of the sami checks: tests that fail on every tree for a reason the tree does not
# own yet. The summary shows each failure as KNOWN (with this reason) or NEW; a unit whose only
# failures are known reads KNOWN, unless a test in it skipped itself and passed as no other user
# (then it is UNKNOWN). An entry whose test passed or no longer exists is listed in the summary to
# be removed, and the summary job fails until it is, so the list only shrinks.
# A flaky entry, whose reason starts with `flaky: `, names a test that fails in some runs and passes
# in others. When it fails, its job runs its whole unit again (set.sh, nextest.sh, ts.sh: the same
# binary or filter, the same threads, the same user), at most twice; its failure reads KNOWN only
# when it passed in such a retry, and NEW when it failed every retry or passed only in a smaller run
# (a race at 4 threads can pass alone). Where a runner gives each test a process of its own
# (nextest), the test's own retry is that process again and counts: sc.py reads nextest's own
# retries from its JUnit report (a test with <flakyFailure> attempts that passed in the end is a
# flaky failure, never a pass; one whose <rerunFailure> retries all failed stays failed). A flaky
# failure with no entry reads NEW. An entry is not listed for removal when its test passes (it
# still is when its test no longer exists).
# The platform rows (macos, windows) are read the same way from each leg's JUnit report, nextest's
# own retry in the same run (the same binary, profile, threads and user, under the run's load). A
# platform test is <binary>::<test> (user runner, unit pi-shell), with " (TIMEOUT)" after it when it
# ran past its time bound, which no entry makes KNOWN. A clippy finding is "<file>: <message>".
# A unit of `*` names the test in any unit of its row, on the rows whose units are shards (ts-ca,
# workspace: sc.py ANY_UNIT_ROWS): a coding-agent shard holds the test files whose sorted index mod
# 10 is the shard's, so a file added before a test moves it to another shard. On the other rows a
# test's name is unique only inside its unit, and sc.py refuses `*` there.
# A known self-skip, whose reason starts with `skips: `, has a sixth field: the start of the skip
# line the test prints (each `{...}` any text). A test that skipped itself reads KNOWN when each of
# its skip lines starts as an entry of its row, user and test says; one user's entry never covers
# the other user, and a unit with any other self-skip (not passed as the other user) is UNKNOWN.
# An entry whose test ran without skipping itself, or printed no line that starts so, is listed
# for removal.
# One per line, tab-separated: <row> <user> <unit> <test> <reason> [<skip line start>].
# Rows: set-runner, set-root, builtins, workspace, ts-small, ts-ca, macos, windows, clippy (sc.py ROWS).
# Source: runs 45245119907 (509a2d77) and 45245136412 (a72018dd); red at both trees.
